messages:
eva_perf: Heads-up — nightly regression after kernel-selector change. 99th p99 latency jumped ~18% on long-context chat workload. perf-bot posted bench in #ci-nightlies.

dan_runtimedev: hmm, which selector rule landed? the dynamic-coalesce one?

eva_perf: yes, merged yesterday (dynamic-coalesce + prefer-fused for small batches). baseline vs HEAD:
```
baseline: 35ms p99, 5.6ms p50
HEAD:     41ms p99, 5.9ms p50
workload: batch sizes vary 1-6, seq_len=2048, kv_cache interleaved layout
```

alice_ml: interesting that p50 barely moved but p99 did. sounds like a tail problem (stragglers). maybe KV access stride causes occasional warp stalls.

eva_perf: I profiled a few tails with nvprof and saw some big variance on sgemm launches and a couple of cache-miss spikes. snippet: 
```
# nvprof summary (truncated)
Time(%)  Calls  Avg(ms)  Name
42.7     120    0.18     fused_flash_attn_kernel_v2
27.3     95     0.05     kv_read_strided
8.9      12     3.2      split_kernel_fallback
```

ben_infra: kv_read_strided worries me. Are we hitting misaligned loads when interleaved layout + odd dtype? any bfloat16 vs fp16 casts?

carla_sre: also check allocator fragmentation. If cache pages aren't 256B-aligned we get extra loads. Have we changed allocator hinting in the new selector?

eva_perf: allocator unchanged. model uses float16. But dynamic-coalesce tries to coalesce small requests across users which creates mixed stride patterns for KV buffers (interleaved per-request). suspect combinatorial stride patterns cause some batches to fall back to split_kernel_fallback.

dan_runtimedev: that aligns with what I saw in the kernel selector logs: when mixed-request shapes present we prefer fused flash for latency, but fused flash assumes contiguous per-batch KV layout. If layout is interleaved we re-route to the paged fallback less efficiently. We didn't instrument that code path enough.

alice_ml: quick mitigation: add a cheap check in selector to prefer separate-contiguous KV when mixed small batches likely. Also add a metric: fallback_count per-model per-minute.

eva_perf: agree. I can add a metric and a debug flag to force contiguous rewriting at request coalescer. Will run a narrow canary for the next nightly.

ben_infra: For longer term, can we make fused kernel handle stride != 1 by reading into a temp contiguous tile (fast path) rather than full fallback? microcopy path:
```
if (stride != 1 && small_batch) {
  tile_into_shared(tmp, src, tile_size);
  call_fused(tmp);
}
```

carla_sre: that temp-copy will add cycles but may reduce variance. worth perf microbenching. add NVTX ranges so we can attribute cost.

dan_runtimedev: I'll add a microbench script (random strides, dtype permutations, batch 1..8, seq 512..2048) and upload results to the perf dashboard. want to see break-even points.

eva_perf: thanks. will flip the debug flag and re-run nightly. if p99 drops back we know selector heuristics caused it. otherwise we'll dig into allocator/page alignment.

perf-bot: nightly/1942102467: regression detected for model chat-2048 on branch main. p99 +17.6%. linked artifacts: s3://redwood-perf/nightlies/1942102467.html

alice_ml: ping @dan_runtimedev @ben_infra - once you have microbench numbers, let's sync tomorrow 10am to pick plan (selector tweak vs kernel temp-copy vs allocator change). :calendar:
